purpose: Echothiophate iodide eye drops are used to treat certain types of glaucoma, a condition where pressure builds up inside your eye. It is also used to treat a specific type of crossed eyes called accommodative esotropia, especially in children. Your doctor may also use it to diagnose certain eye conditions.
how_it_works: Your eye has a natural chemical that controls how your eye muscles work. This medicine blocks an enzyme that normally breaks down that chemical, causing the pupil to get smaller and helping fluid drain better from your eye. By improving drainage, the pressure inside your eye goes down, which helps protect your vision.
common_side_effects: Your eyes may sting, burn, or feel irritated when you first put in the drops. Your vision might be blurry, especially in dim light, and your pupils will get very small. Some people get headaches, brow aches, or notice their eyelids twitch. You may also be more sensitive to bright light.
warnings: This medicine can affect how your body breaks down certain anesthesia drugs used during surgery, so always tell your doctor and dentist you are using these drops before any procedure. Do not use it if you have certain inflammatory eye conditions without your doctor's guidance. Long-term use can increase the risk of developing cataracts. Keep all follow-up eye appointments so your doctor can monitor your eye pressure and overall eye health.
typical_dosing: Usually one drop is placed in the affected eye once or twice a day, or as directed by your eye doctor. Use it at the same time each day to get the best results. Never use more drops than your doctor prescribed, as this medicine is very potent and small changes in dose can make a big difference.
